sentences.text:
-Vs-
Kadan Kisku & Anr.
Mr. Rajesh Singh, Mr. Aniruddha Singh .... For the Petitioner.
By the order impugned the application filed by the insurance company praying for dismissal of the application filed under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 stood rejected.

Mr. Singh, learned advocate appearing for the insurance company petitioner draws the attention of the Court to the provision laid down under Section 166(3) of the 1988 Act wherein it has been stated that no application for compensation shall be entertained unless it is made within six months of the occurrence of the accidence.
Mr. Singh submits that in the case on hand the application for compensation has been filed after a lapse of six months from the date of accident.
It is not in dispute that the application filed by the claimant in the case on hand was under the provisions of Section 164 of the 1988 Act and not under Section 166(1) of the 1988 Act.
The question that arises for consideration is whether the time bar incorporated under Section 166(3) of the 1988 Act would apply also two applications under Section 164.
This court feels that the opposite parties are to be heard on such issue.
The petitioner is directed to serve a copy of this application upon the opposite parties herein by registered speed post with acknowledgement due and file an affidavit-of-service on the next date.
List this matter under the heading "Motion" in the Monthly list of September, 2025.
It is however made clear that pendency of this application shall not preclude the motor accident claim tribunal from proceedings with the claim application in the meantime.

(Hiranmay Bhattacharyya, J.)
